newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi willing to sell Nina Ricci stake.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi willing to sell Nina Ricci stake.

text.p: Pharmaceuticals and beauty products group Sanofi would unload its 49.9 percent stake in Nina Ricci if the perfume house's founders decided to sell, a spokesman for Sanofi said on Tuesday.
"If the majority shareholder decided to sell, we would sell at the same time," the spokesman said.
Sanofi's stock was up 5.88 percent at 612 francs at 0945 GMT after the newspaper La Tribune reported that Nina Ricci's staff council was told last Friday that Sanofi was keen to sell.

Sanofi, a unit of Elf Aquitaine, has itself been the object of speculation since the energy group said last year that it was willing to cut its stake to below 50 percent and find a merger partner for Sanofi.
"Sanofi's asset selling raises expectations that Elf is preparing to sell (its stake in Sanofi)," a broker said.
Another trader said brokers were raising their ratings and targets on Sanofi.
The majority owners of Nina Ricci, best known for its L'Air du Temps classic fragrance, are Nina Ricci chairman Gilles Fuchs and his family.
Nina Ricci generated 1.1 billion francs of turnover in 1996 but has lost money for two years on its perfume business, La Tribune said.
